html:
In 1415 Emperor Manuel II rebuilt the Hexamilion, a wall about six Roman miles long across the Isthmus of Corinth, to shield the Byzantine lands of the Morea from the Ottomans.

The wall was first built in the early 400s under the Eastern Roman emperor Theodosius II, against invaders from the north. By Manuel's time it was a ruin. He came in person and had it rebuilt quickly with forced labour, which angered local landowners.

It did not hold long. Ottoman troops broke through in 1423 and again in later raids. Constantine, then ruler at Mistra, restored it in 1444, but in 1446 Murad II battered it with cannon and stormed it. After that the Morea paid tribute, and in 1460 the Ottomans took it. The later Corinth Canal cuts the isthmus near where the wall ran.
sum: In 1415 Emperor Manuel II rebuilt the Hexamilion, a wall about six Roman miles long across the Isthmus of Corinth, to shield the Byzantine lands of the Morea from the Ottomans.
